data.title: MCPDisCo: Seesaw-Mitigated Tuning for MCP-Native Agents
data.description: arXiv:2610.14956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Model Context Protocol provides a shared interaction substrate for the agentic web, allowing heterogeneous services to expose capabilities through a standardized interface. Learning to use this ecosystem entails a hierarchy of capabilities: tool-format skills, server-level transfer, and cross-server composition. We present MCPDisCo, an ecosystem-scale reinforcement learning framework for MCP-native agents. Using a Thought-Markov Decision Process (Thought-MDP), the framework explicitly represents internal reasoning alongside routing, execution, and termination and trains on real-server, long-horizon interactions spanning 70 MCP servers and 527 tools across six domains. We study the reasoning--tool seesaw, a joint-learning failure mode in which improvement in one objective can accompany deterioration in the other. To mitigate potential interference, MCPDisCo combines token-masked reward attribution with bidirectional gradient surgery: the former separates direct supervision for reasoning and action spans, while the latter removes conflicting components from both objective gradients in shared parameters. MCPDisCo achieves higher success with fewer chain-of-thought tokens. On the out-of-distribution MCP-Atlas and the GAIA benchmark, MCPDisCo maintains monotone gains, confirming that the learned behavior generalizes beyond the training server distribution and broader agentic tasks. Model weight and implementation are available.
data.author: Kounianhua Du, Jianxing Liu, Shuai Shao, Ke Li, Xing Sun, Weinan Zhang
